description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec 6.6.5's inline `reference` scope: 'an inline Expression whose free variables are the domain dimension names'. For a field shaped over index sets the dimension names are the asserted variable's `shape` entries, each bound at every grid point to the 1-based position along its axis (the index space `coords` reads, convention 1). Before this category all three executing bindings evaluated the reference as ONE build-time array expression and sampled it per cell, so a dimension name mentioned free was simply unbound (Rust E_TREEWALK_UNBOUND_NAME, Python 'Unresolved symbol', Julia UNBOUND_VARIABLE) and authors had to spell every reference as an explicit `faq(i from x; ...)` gather. The fixture asserts one exact decay field through the free-name analytic form (twice: against the field itself, and against the same shape scaled by exp(-1), whose relative L2 error is e-1 exactly), a table lookup by the dimension name, the explicit gather, and a gather that rebinds the dimension name as its own loop symbol (which must NOT be wrapped a second time), plus a reference-free `mean` as the regression guard; all must agree on the golden actuals. Julia is the reference binding and minted golden/reference_dimension_names.json through its own `run_pde_tests`. The right-hand side is linear decay of a per-cell constant field, so every pinned solver family reproduces exp(-t) to the assertion tolerances.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner

tolerances.note: The 1e-11 assertion_atol of every sibling pde_inline_* category. Assertion 2 originally sampled t=1, which made its actual (the relative L2 error of u(t=1) against the analytic reference) the time-integrator's own residual — Julia Tsit5 left 1.8e-14, Python RK45 5.2e-11 at the pinned rtol=1e-12/atol=1e-14 — and forced a 1e-9 atol on the whole category. It now samples t=0 against the same reference shape scaled by exp(-1), so its actual is the scale mismatch alone, e-1 exactly, computed in build-time arithmetic with no solver in the loop. What remains at t=1 is the table Linf_error (O(64), gated by assertion_rtol) and the reference-free mean, which is ~0 to roundoff in every binding because the RHS is per-cell linear decay: every cell is scaled by the SAME integrator factor, so the mean of an antisymmetric initial field stays antisymmetric and the residual cancels rather than accumulating.

assertions.reference_form: free dimension name, analytic, scaled by exp(-1) at t=0
table lookup indexed by the dimension name
gather rebinding the dimension name as its loop symbol
